speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have shortness of breath, increased abdominal girth, and a large ovarian mass. To determine the cause of your symptoms, I need to ask you some questions. Are you experiencing any abdominal pain or changes in your bowel or bladder habits?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old nulliparous woman. The patient reports experiencing shortness of breath and noticeable increase in abdominal size over the past month. She denies any significant medical history, previous surgeries, or use of medications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Ovarian malignancy (likely epithelial ovarian cancer) causing malignant ascites and compressive atelectasis. The triad of a large ovarian mass, rapid increase in abdominal girth (ascites), and shortness of breath in a 40-year-old woman is highly suggestive of advanced ovarian cancer. Immediate evaluation with a CA-125 level and pelvic ultrasound/CT is required to confirm and stage the disease.
